phrases.text: So welcome back again.
Time for one more problem. Now, in this problem, we are given that the downstream speed of a boat is twenty-four kilometer per hour. The upstream speed of the same boat
is sixteen kilometer per hour.
The question is asking us to find the speed of the current. Now, first,
let us assume the speed of the boat in still water is
b kilometer
per hour,
and the speed of the current is c kilometer
per hour.
Now, let us understand what downstream and upstream mean.
Imagine that the river is flowing in this direction.
The boat itself can move at b kilometer per hour in still water.
The river is also flowing at c kilometer per hour.
Now, when the boat moves in the same direction as the river,
both the boat and the current help each other,
so their speeds get added.
That is why
downstream speed is equal to speed of the boat in still water plus
speed of the current,
or simply b plus
c. Now, let us look at the opposite case. When the boat moves against the flow of the river,
the current tries to slow the boat down,
so the speed of the current gets subtracted from the speed of the boat.
That is why
upstream speed is equal to speed of the boat in still water
minus speed of the current,
or simply
b minus
c.
Now, let us use the given values.
The downstream speed is twenty-four,
so b plus c is equal to twenty-four.
The upstream speed is sixteen, so b minus c is equal to sixteen. Now we need to find the speed of the current, which is c.
So let us subtract the second equation from the first.
On the left side,
b plus c minus b minus c. The b terms cancel each other, so we are left with two c. On the right side,
twenty-four minus sixteen, which is eight.
So two c is equal to eight.
Dividing both sides by two, we get c is equal to four.
So the speed of the current is
four kilometer per hour.
Hence, the correct answer is option D.
